questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. In the flesh

questions.solution:

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'In bodily form'.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. Cast someone adrift
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Cast someone adrift

options.text: To leave someone without any support or purpose
options.html: To leave someone without any support or purpose

options.text: To blame someone for one’s mistakes
options.html: To blame someone for one’s mistakes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'To leave someone without any support or purpose '.

Key Points

  • The phrase "Cast someone adrift" means to abandon or isolate someone, often leaving them without support, resources, or a clear sense of direction.
  • It comes from a nautical term where a boat is let loose to drift without being controlled or anchored.
  • To leave someone without any support or purpose: This captures the essence of the idiom "cast someone adrift".
  • It refers to abandoning someone without any assistance or clear path.(किसी को बिना किसी सहारे या उद्देश्य के छोड़ देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'To leave someone without any support or purpose'.

Additional Information

  • Looking at the provided options:
    • To change plan suddenly: It implies a sudden alteration in previously decided plans.(अचानक योजना बदल देना)
    • Call someone repeatedly: It refers to the act of continuously calling someone, possibly to the point of annoyance.(किसी को बार-बार बुलाना)
    • To blame someone for one’s mistakes: It refers to the act of shifting the responsibility or blame for one's own errors onto someone else.(अपनी गलतियों के लिए किसी अन्य को दोषी ठहराना)

questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. As hard as nails

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Physically or mentally tough​'.

Key Points

  • The phrase "As hard as nails" best corresponds to option 3: "Physically or mentally tough."
  • The idiom "As hard as nails" is used to describe a person who is very tough or uncompromising, both in a physical and psychological sense.
  • This phrase is often used to describe someone who is not easily upset or hurt, and can handle difficult situations well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Physically or mentally tough'.

Additional Information

  • Let's take a look at the other options:
    • "To be stubborn" (जिद्दी होना) refers to a person who is not willing to change their ideas or to consider anyone else's reasons or arguments.
    • "To feel no pain" (दर्द नहीं महसूस करना) suggests someone who is insensitive to pain. While it might be a quality of someone who is "hard as nails," it does not encompass the whole meaning of the phrase.
    • "Hard working" (मेहनती) refers to a person who puts a lot of effort into their work. While a person who is "as hard as nails" might also be hard-working, this doesn't capture the full sense of toughness and resilience implied by the idiom.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom for the following statement. The manager was punished for his negligence in work.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following statement.

The manager was punished for his negligence in work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Bid defiance" means to openly resist or refuse to obey. (अवज्ञा करना)
    • Example: The rebel leader bid defiance to the new laws imposed by the government.
  • "Burn one’s boats" signifies taking an action which makes it impossible to return to the previous situation; a point of no return. (नावों को जलाना - वापसी का कोई मार्ग न छोड़ना)
    • Example: By quitting his job and moving to another country, he has truly burned his boats.
  • "Bolt from the blue" refers to something happening completely unexpectedly, similar to a sudden and unforeseen lightning strike from a clear sky. (आकस्मिक और अप्रत्याशित)
    • Example: The sudden resignation of the CEO was a bolt from the blue for the company.
  • "Bring to book" means to punish someone or make them accountable for their actions. (किसी को उसके कार्यों के लिए दंडित करना या जवाबदेह बनाना)
    • Example: The fraudulent investor was finally brought to book after years of illegal activities.
  • Hence, relating to the statement about the manager being punished for his negligence, the most appropriate idiom is "Bring to book."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Bid defiance (अवज्ञा करना): It is about refusing to obey or showing resistance.
    • Example: The citizens bid defiance to the unfair regulations imposed by the authorities.
  • Burn one’s boats (नावों को जलाना - वापसी का कोई मार्ग न छोड़ना): Taking irreversible actions.
    • Example: She burned her boats by selling all her shares to start her own company.
  • Bolt from the blue (आकस्मिक और अप्रत्याशित): Something that happens unexpectedly.
    • Example: Winning the lottery was a bolt from the blue for him.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence. He was alone and knew the dangers ahead during his journey, but he tried to keep up his confidence.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence.

He was alone and knew the dangers ahead during his journey, but he tried to keep up his confidence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: whistled in the dark.

Key Points

  • The phrase "to keep up his confidence" refers to maintaining one's self-assurance and belief in oneself despite challenging circumstances. (आत्मविश्वास बनाए रखना)
    • Example: Even when the odds were against her, she did everything she could to keep up her confidence.
  • "Whistled in the dark" is an idiom that means trying to remain brave or pretending to be unafraid in a scary or uncertain situation; it implies an attempt to keep up one's spirits. (डर के बावजूद साहस बनाए रखना)
    • Example: He whistled in the dark as he walked through the abandoned house, trying not to let his fear show.
  • Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom for "tried to keep up his confidence" is "whistled in the dark".

Therefore, the correct answer is: whistled in the dark.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Made of sterner stuff (अधिक मजबूत बनाया गया): Refers to someone who is very strong in character, especially in a difficult situation.
    • Example: Despite the setbacks, she proved she was made of sterner stuff and persevered.
  • Stepped up his game (अपने खेल को बेहतर बनाया): To improve performance or quality in response to a challenge.
    • Example: After receiving feedback, he stepped up his game and delivered an outstanding presentation.
  • Wouldn’t be caught dead (किसी भी स्थिति में नहीं पाया जाएगा): Used to express strong dislike or disapproval towards something.
    • Example: He’s so particular about his appearance; he wouldn’t be caught dead wearing something out of fashion.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Hush money (चुप रहने के लिए दी गई रिश्वत): Money paid to someone to keep them silent about something.
    • Example: The company paid hush money to the whistleblower to prevent the scandal from coming to light.
  • Having one’s cake and eating it too (दोनों चीज़ें एक साथ चाहना): Trying to have two incompatible things at the same time.
    • Example: You can't be in a relationship and flirt with others; that's having one’s cake and eating it too.
  • Making a fuss out of something (किसी बात को लेकर हंगामा करना): Complaining or getting upset about something trivial.
    • Example: She’s always making a fuss out of nothing; it's really annoying.
